rootCause: createIndexer built LogCursor without confirmations, so the SDK default of 0n saved the cursor through eth_blockNumber. An empty eth_getLogs from a lagging replica still advanced index_cursor.last_block and could skip later ProofAccepted and KeyReleased logs. The SDK LogCursor already accepts confirmations. Funding receipt reads were not the broken path and were not changed.

change.indexer: IndexerOptions.confirmations is optional. createIndexer passes it through to LogCursor. Omitted stays the SDK default of 0n.
change.server: Startup passes confirmations 3n when chain.mode is arc and 0n otherwise. It uses the existing ApiChain mode. No CHAIN_MODE variable was added. cursorStart remains INDEX_FROM_BLOCK or 0. maxRange is still omitted so LogCursor keeps its 10000-block window.

preserved: Arc chain-id check still runs before getBlockNumber and getLogs.
Log windows stay at the SDK default of 10000 blocks. One tick with maxWindowsPerTick 1 and head 20000 still reads through block 9999.
Event rows and the cursor still commit in one transaction. A thrown getLogs leaves both tables empty.
Recovery, signer policy, funding-receipt handling, and the worker were not edited.

embeddedCallerLimitation.productionStartup: chainFromEnv returns createApiArcChain whenever CHAIN_RPC_URL is set, so a configured server chain is arc mode. There is no production startup path that builds a simulated chain.
embeddedCallerLimitation.howSimulatedZeroWasTested: The server test rewrites only the test double of createApiArcChain to mode simulated and expects confirmations 0n. That mock is not a new server mode switch.
embeddedCallerLimitation.embeddedCallers: Callers that construct createIndexer themselves and omit confirmations stay at 0n. The T11 submission harness does that and was not refactored. Its single default-suite test passed.

persistedCursors.requirement: An approved reindex or a fresh local database is required before this margin can recover history that an already-advanced index_cursor.last_block has skipped. New empty cursors stay three blocks behind head on arc. This change does not rewind or delete stored cursors.

red.command: cd commerce && pnpm --filter @ubc26/api exec vitest run test/unit/arc-reader-indexer.test.ts test/unit/server-provenance.test.ts
red.when: After the regressions existed and before indexer.ts or server.ts were edited.
failures: Lagging getLogs with confirmations 3n saved last_block 10. The test required 7, which is head 10 minus 3, so the later ProofAccepted and KeyReleased logs would have been skipped.
Arc server startup called createIndexer with confirmations undefined. The test required 3n. cursorStart stayed 0n and maxRange stayed unset.
The simulated-mode startup double called createIndexer with confirmations undefined. The test required 0n.
red.characterizationCorrection: An earlier run of the same command, still before production edits, failed 4 tests. The extra failure expected the omitted-confirmations cursor to stay at 10 after head moved to 13. A 0n cursor correctly advanced to 13 through the empty window and stored no events. That expectation was changed to 13 before the recorded red run. No production code had been edited.

diffSummary: commerce/api/src/indexer.ts: added optional confirmations on IndexerOptions and passed opts.confirmations into the LogCursor constructor. Chain-id guard, in-memory pending cursor, transactional persist, and maxRange passthrough are unchanged.

commerce/api/src/server.ts: the startup createIndexer call now sets confirmations to 3n when chain.mode is arc and 0n otherwise. Interval, cursor start, and the absent maxRange override are unchanged.

commerce/api/test/unit/arc-reader-indexer.test.ts: added the lagging acceptance/release regression, the omitted-confirmations simulated caller case, the 10000-block cap, a failed getLogs case, and the wrong-chain case with confirmations set. Existing assertions were not weakened.

commerce/api/test/unit/server-provenance.test.ts: arc startup expects 3n; a test-only simulated mode rewrite expects 0n. The existing rejection tests still require that an arc chain with a simulated engine opens no database, starts no indexer, and does not listen.
No other source, migration, database, worker, signer, or document file was edited for this fix.
